title: GNN-CB: A Graph Neural Network Competition Benchmark for Human and LLM Evaluation
title_zh: GNN-CB：面向人类与大型语言模型评估的图神经网络竞赛基准

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on coding and reasoning benchmarks; however, their ability to solve graph-structured machine learning problems remains largely unexplored. In particular, no benchmark currently evaluates whether LLMs can autonomously solve end-to-end Graph Neural Network (GNN) coding tasks under realistic competition settings. To address this gap, this paper introduces GNN-CB , the first competition-based benchmark for evaluating both humans and LLMs on GNN coding tasks. GNN-CB consists of 18 curated competitions spanning node-, edge-, and graph-level prediction across diverse graph categories, domains, and difficulty tiers. All submissions are evaluated through a unified automated pipeline with hidden test sets and standardized scoring. Human participants solve tasks under controlled competition constraints, while LLMs are evaluated using a frozen zero-shot prompting protocol based on a plan-then-code paradigm with bounded execute-and-repair loops. The benchmark additionally supports both non-agent and autonomous agent-based evaluation within the same protocol. Under our evaluated protocol, LLMs rarely match Human Top performance and show less stable performance across competitions. No single model dominates: a few competitions are won by LLMs, yet humans still hold the top score on most tasks. We release GNN-CB as a living benchmark with automated evaluation infrastructure, dynamic leaderboards, and reproducible execution pipelines. Beyond benchmarking, GNN-CB provides a practice-oriented resource for studying GNN implementation across progressively diverse graph-learning tasks. The benchmark and evaluation framework are publicly available at https://basiralab.github.io/GNN-CB/ .
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）在编码和推理基准测试中展现了强大的性能；然而，它们在解决图结构机器学习问题方面的能力仍 largely 未被探索。 特别地，目前没有任何基准测试能够评估 LLM 是否能在真实的竞赛环境中自主完成端到端的图神经网络（GNN）编码任务。 为了填补这一空白，本文提出了 GNN-CB——首个基于竞赛的基准测试，用于评估人类和 LLM 在 GNN 编码任务上的表现。 GNN-CB 包含 18 项精心设计的竞赛，涵盖节点、边和图级别的预测任务，涉及多样的图类别、领域和难度等级。 所有提交的答案都将通过统一的自动化流程进行评估，该流程包含隐藏测试集和标准化的评分机制。 人类参与者在受控的竞赛约束条件下完成任务，而 LLM 则基于“规划-编码”范式，在受限的执行与修复循环下，通过冻结的零样本提示协议进行评估。 该基准测试还支持在同一协议框架内，对非智能体模式和自主智能体模式进行联合评估。 在我们评估的协议下，LLM 很少能达到人类顶尖水平，且在不同竞赛中的表现稳定性也较低。 没有任何单一模型占据绝对优势：少数竞赛由 LLM 获胜，但人类在大多数任务中仍保持最高得分。 我们将 GNN-CB 作为一个动态更新的基准测试发布，包含自动化评估基础设施、实时排行榜和可复现的执行流程。 除了基准测试功能外，GNN-CB 还提供了一个实践导向的资源，可用于研究在逐步多样化的图学习任务中实现 GNN 的方法。 该基准测试及评估框架可在 https://basiralab.github.io/GNN-CB/ 公开获取。

paragraphs.en: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are widely used for learning over graph-structured data in domains such as molecular modeling, recommender systems, social networks, neuroimaging, and knowledge graphs ( Gilmer et al., 2017 ; Hamilton et al., 2017 ; Li et al., 2018 ; Ying et al., 2018 ; Li et al., 2021 ; Dauparas et al., 2022 ; Schlichtkrull et al., 2018 ) . Unlike conventional coding tasks, GNN problems require understanding graph topology, building relational pipelines, selecting message-passing architectures, and optimizing under task-specific constraints, making them more challenging than isolated algorithmic tasks.

paragraphs.en: Despite the growing importance of graph machine learning, no existing benchmark evaluates whether LLMs can autonomously solve realistic end-to-end GNN coding tasks. Benchmarks such as HumanEval ( Chen et al., 2021 ) , CodeContests ( Li et al., 2022 ) , SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2023 ) , and BigCodeBench ( Zhuo et al., 2024 ) focus on algorithmic reasoning or software engineering workflows without graph-learning components, while graph benchmarks such as OGB ( Hu et al., 2020 ) and LRGB ( Dwivedi et al., 2022 ) are designed to evaluate the predictive performance of GNN models rather than their implementation.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管图机器学习的重要性日益凸显，但目前尚无任何基准测试能够评估大型语言模型（LLM）是否具备自主解决真实端到端图神经网络（GNN）编码任务的能力。 HumanEval（Chen 等人，2021）、CodeContests（Li 等人，2022）、SWE-bench（Jimenez 等人，2023）和 BigCodeBench（Zhuo 等人，2024）等基准测试主要关注算法推理或软件工程工作流程，且未包含图学习组件；而 OGB（Hu 等人，2020）和 LRGB（Dwivedi 等人，2022）等图相关基准测试则旨在评估 GNN 模型的预测性能，而非其实现过程。

paragraphs.en: To ensure fair and reproducible assessment, we define three complementary protocols: (i) competition design, (ii) human evaluation, and (iii) LLM evaluation. Human participants solve tasks under controlled competition constraints with fixed computational budgets and limited submissions. LLMs are evaluated using a frozen zero-shot prompting protocol based on a structured plan-then-code paradigm with bounded execute-and-repair loops. The benchmark additionally supports both non-agent and autonomous agent-based evaluation settings within the same protocol.
paragraphs.zh: 为确保评估的公平性和可重复性，我们定义了三种互补的协议：(i) 竞赛设计、(ii) 人类评估和 (iii) LLM 评估。 人类参与者在受控的竞赛约束条件下完成任务，其计算预算固定且提交次数有限。 LLM 的评估采用固定的零样本提示协议，该协议基于结构化的“先规划后编码”范式，并包含有界执行与修复循环。 此外，该基准在同一协议内还支持非智能体和基于自主智能体的两种评估模式。

paragraphs.en: Our contributions are summarized as follows. (i) GNN-CB is introduced as the first competition-based benchmark for evaluating both humans and LLMs on GNN coding tasks. (ii) The benchmark contains 18 human-curated competitions spanning diverse graph categories, application domains, and difficulty tiers under unified hidden-test evaluation protocols. (iii) A controlled LLM evaluation framework is proposed based on frozen prompting, plan-then-code generation, and bounded execute-and-repair loops, supporting both agent-based and non-agent settings. (iv) Evaluation of human participants and LLMs enables systematic analysis of performance variability, task difficulty, and implementation challenges in realistic GNN coding environments. (v) GNN-CB is released as a living benchmark with automated evaluation infrastructure, reproducible pipelines, and dynamic leaderboards to support future research on the capabilities and limitations of LLMs as autonomous GNN engineers, as well as serving as a structured resource for hands-on GNN practice across progressively diverse graph-learning tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的贡献总结如下。 (i) GNN-CB 被提出作为首个基于竞赛的基准，用于评估人类和大型语言模型（LLM）在 GNN 编码任务上的表现。 (ii) 该基准包含 18 项由人类精心策划的竞赛，涵盖多样的图类别、应用领域和难度等级，并采用统一的隐藏测试评估协议。 (iii) 我们提出了一种受控的 LLM 评估框架，基于固定提示、计划-编码生成以及受限的执行与修复循环，支持智能体和非智能体的两种设置。 (iv) 对人类参与者和 LLM 的评估使得能够系统性地分析在真实 GNN 编码环境中表现的可变性、任务难度及实现挑战。 (v) GNN-CB 作为一个动态更新的基准发布，包含自动化评估基础设施、可复现的流程以及动态排行榜，以支持未来关于 LLM 作为自主 GNN 工程师的能力与局限性的研究，同时为逐步多样化的图学习任务提供结构化的实践资源。

paragraphs.en: Recent benchmarks have significantly advanced evaluation of LLM-based code generation and reasoning. HumanEval ( Chen et al., 2021 ) and CodeContests ( Li et al., 2022 ) introduced standardized evaluation for functional correctness and competitive programming. Later works extended evaluation across programming languages and stricter testing settings, including HumanEval-X ( Peng et al., 2024 ) , MultiPL-E ( Cassano et al., 2023 ) , and EvalPlus ( Liu et al., 2023 ) . More realistic software engineering benchmarks such as DS-1000 ( Lai et al., 2023 ) , SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2023 ) , BigCodeBench ( Zhuo et al., 2024 ) , and LiveCodeBench ( Jain et al., 2024 ) evaluate repository-level reasoning, data science workflows, and instruction-following capabilities.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的基准测试显著推动了基于大型语言模型（LLM）的代码生成与推理能力的评估。 HumanEval（Chen 等人，2021）和 CodeContests（Li 等人，2022）引入了针对功能正确性和编程竞赛的标准评估方法。 后续研究将评估范围扩展至多种编程语言和更严格的测试环境，包括 HumanEval-X（Peng 等人，2024）、MultiPL-E（Cassano 等人，2023）和 EvalPlus（Liu 等人，2023）。 更贴近实际软件工程场景的基准测试，如 DS-1000（Lai 等人，2023）、SWE-bench（Jimenez 等人，2023）、BigCodeBench（Zhuo 等人，2024）和 LiveCodeBench（Jain 等人，2024），则用于评估代码仓库级别的推理能力、数据科学工作流程以及指令遵循能力。

sents.en: Recent benchmarks have significantly advanced evaluation of LLM-based code generation and reasoning.

sents.en: HumanEval ( Chen et al., 2021 ) and CodeContests ( Li et al., 2022 ) introduced standardized evaluation for functional correctness and competitive programming.

sents.en: Later works extended evaluation across programming languages and stricter testing settings, including HumanEval-X ( Peng et al., 2024 ) , MultiPL-E ( Cassano et al., 2023 ) , and EvalPlus ( Liu et al., 2023 ) .
sents.zh: 后续研究将评估范围扩展至多种编程语言和更严格的测试环境，包括 HumanEval-X（Peng 等人，2024）、MultiPL-E（Cassano 等人，2023）和 EvalPlus（Liu 等人，2023）。

sents.en: More realistic software engineering benchmarks such as DS-1000 ( Lai et al., 2023 ) , SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2023 ) , BigCodeBench ( Zhuo et al., 2024 ) , and LiveCodeBench ( Jain et al., 2024 ) evaluate repository-level reasoning, data science workflows, and instruction-following capabilities.
sents.zh: 更贴近实际软件工程场景的基准测试，如 DS-1000（Lai 等人，2023）、SWE-bench（Jimenez 等人，2023）、BigCodeBench（Zhuo 等人，2024）和 LiveCodeBench（Jain 等人，2024），则用于评估代码仓库级别的推理能力、数据科学工作流程以及指令遵循能力。

paragraphs.en: Graph machine learning benchmarks have standardized evaluation for graph neural networks (GNNs). The Open Graph Benchmark (OGB) ( Hu et al., 2020 ) provides datasets and evaluation protocols for node-, edge-, and graph-level prediction tasks, while Benchmarking GNNs ( Dwivedi et al., 2023 ) and LRGB ( Dwivedi et al., 2022 ) focus on structural generalization and long-range graph dependencies. However, these benchmarks do not assess whether LLMs can perform at a human level on GNN competitions.
paragraphs.zh: 图机器学习基准测试为图神经网络（GNN）提供了标准化的评估方法。 Open Graph Benchmark（OGB）（Hu 等人，2020）为节点级、边级和图级预测任务提供了数据集和评估协议，而 Benchmarking GNNs（Dwivedi 等人，2023）和 LRGB（Dwivedi 等人，2022）则专注于结构泛化能力和长距离图依赖关系。 然而，这些基准测试并未评估大型语言模型（LLM）是否能在 GNN 竞赛中达到人类水平的表现。

paragraphs.en: GNN-CB bridges these two research directions by introducing a competition-based benchmark for GNN coding tasks, supporting unified evaluation of both human participants and LLMs under controlled and reproducible conditions.
paragraphs.zh: GNN-CB 通过为 GNN 编码任务引入一种基于竞争的基准测试，将这两个研究方向连接起来，从而支持在受控且可复现的条件下对人类参与者和大型语言模型（LLM）进行统一评估。

paragraphs.en: GNN-CB is a competition-based benchmark for evaluating GNN coding tasks under standardized settings. Unlike traditional code-generation benchmarks centered on isolated functions or short algorithmic problems, GNN-CB targets repository-level graph learning workflows where participants or LLMs must build complete pipelines spanning data processing, graph construction, architecture design, optimization, and hidden-test prediction generation.
paragraphs.zh: GNN-CB 是一个基于竞赛的基准测试，用于在标准化设置下评估 GNN 编码任务。 与以孤立函数或简短算法问题为核心的传统代码生成基准测试不同，GNN-CB 针对的是仓库级别的图学习工作流程，其中参与者或 LLM 必须构建涵盖数据处理、图构建、架构设计、优化以及隐藏测试预测生成的完整流程。

paragraphs.en: The competition design protocol organizes benchmark tasks across diverse graph learning settings. The benchmark contains 18 independent competitions spanning node classification, edge prediction, graph classification, and graph regression tasks (Figure 1 ). Competitions are organized along two axes: graph category and difficulty tier. The benchmark covers seven graph categories, including homogeneous , heterogeneous , temporal , spatial , hierarchical , molecular , and generalization graphs. Competitions are additionally grouped into Easy , Medium and Hard difficulty tiers based on implementation complexity, architectural requirements, and observed human performance. Table 1 summarizes all benchmark competitions, including graph categories, dataset scales, feature dimensionalities, application domains, and evaluation metrics. Detailed dataset specifications and repository descriptions are provided in Appendix A .
paragraphs.zh: 竞赛设计协议在多样化的图学习设置中组织基准任务。 该基准包含 18 项独立竞赛，涵盖节点分类、边预测、图分类和图回归任务（图 1）。 竞赛沿两个维度组织：图类别和难度等级。 该基准覆盖七类图，包括同构图、异构图、时序图、空间图、层次图、分子图和泛化图。 竞赛还根据实现复杂性、架构要求和观察到的人类表现，进一步分为简单、中等和困难三个难度等级。 表 1 总结了所有基准竞赛，包括图类别、数据集规模、特征维度、应用领域和评估指标。 详细的数据集规格和仓库描述见附录 A。

paragraphs.en: Each competition is associated with a dedicated repository that specifies the task, submission format, evaluation metrics, and leaderboard configuration. paragraphs.en: The human evaluation protocol measures participant performance under standardized computational and submission constraints. Participants solve each competition independently using only GNN models, without external solutions, and submit a single final prediction file evaluated through the same automated hidden-test pipeline used for LLMs. LLM usage during the human track is restricted to low-level utility support without exposure to task-specific benchmark information. More detailed protocol and participant information are provided in Appendix B . Participants represent 18 universities across 12 countries (Figure 6 , Appendix B ), ensuring geographic diversity in benchmark design and human performance evaluation.

paragraphs.en: GNN-CB evaluates LLMs under a controlled and reproducible protocol designed to measure repository-grounded graph learning ability rather than prompt-engineering performance. All models are evaluated using a frozen prompt template shared across all competitions, without task-specific tuning or adaptive prompting ( Zhuo et al., 2024 ) . As illustrated in Figure 2 , repository information is converted into a standardized prompt through slot filling ( Jain et al., 2024 ) , after which the model generates a structured reasoning plan and an executable code following a plan-then-code paradigm ( Jiang et al., 2024 ) . The generated solution is executed locally in a controlled environment and optionally refined through bounded execute-and-repair iterations ( Yang et al., 2024 ) . Final predictions are evaluated on hidden test sets using the same automated infrastructure used for human participants, enabling direct and fair comparison under identical conditions. The protocol consists of four components: (i) frozen prompt instantiation, (ii) plan-then-code generation, (iii) execution and repair, and (iv) evaluation settings.
paragraphs.zh: GNN-CB 在受控且可复现的协议下评估 LLM，该协议旨在衡量基于代码库的图学习能力，而非提示工程性能。 所有模型均使用在所有竞赛中共享的固定提示模板进行评估，不进行任务特定的调整或自适应提示（Zhuo 等人，2024）。 如图 2 所示，代码库信息通过槽位填充转换为标准化提示（Jain 等人，2024），随后模型按照“先规划后编码”的范式生成结构化推理计划和可执行代码（Jiang 等人，2024）。 生成的解决方案在受控环境中本地执行，并可选择通过有界执行与修复迭代进行优化（Yang 等人，2024）。 最终预测在隐藏测试集上进行评估，并使用与人类参与者相同的自动化基础设施，从而在完全相同的条件下实现直接且公平的对比。 该协议包含四个组成部分：(i) 固定提示实例化、(ii) “先规划后编码”生成、(iii) 执行与修复，以及 (iv) 评估设置。

paragraphs.en: Given the instantiated prompt, the model generates: (i) a high-level reasoning plan and (ii) an executable code. This plan-then-code strategy ( Jiang et al., 2024 ) encourages explicit reasoning before implementation and reduces common failures such as invalid pipelines, hallucinated APIs, or malformed submissions. The accompanying code implements the complete pipeline as a standalone executable solution. A representative plan-then-code output is shown in Figure 9 in Appendix C .

paragraphs.en: GNN-CB supports two complementary execution modes: non-agent and agent-based . In the non-agent mode, a lightweight orchestration script instantiates the frozen prompt with repository-derived slots, dispatches the API request, parses the response into <plan> and <code> blocks, executes the resulting solution.py under the CPU-only environment, and feeds runtime tracebacks back into the prompt for a bounded number of repair iterations; a simplified version of this control loop is reproduced in Listing 2 of Appendix C . In the agent-based mode, an autonomous coding system inspects repository contents, generates an executable solution, runs it, and iteratively repairs failures without human intervention, using the same execute-and-repair budget. Both modes consume identical repository information, enforce the same execution constraints, and submit through the same automated hidden-test pipeline, so that observed performance differences reflect the model’s reasoning and implementation ability rather than prompt-engineering effort or orchestration design.
paragraphs.zh: GNN-CB 支持两种互补的执行模式：非智能体模式和基于智能体的模式。 在非智能体模式下，一个轻量级的编排脚本会利用仓库中获取的槽位来实例化冻结提示，发送 API 请求，将响应解析为 <plan> 和 <code> 块，在仅使用 CPU 的环境中执行生成的 solution.py，并将运行时回溯反馈到提示中，进行有限次数的修复迭代；这种控制循环的简化版本在附录 C 的列表 2 中重现。 在基于智能体的模式下，一个自主编码系统会检查仓库内容，生成可执行方案，运行该方案，并在无需人工干预的情况下迭代修复故障，同时使用相同的执行与修复预算。 两种模式均使用相同的仓库信息、遵循相同的执行约束，并通过相同的自动化隐藏测试流程提交，因此观察到的性能差异反映了模型本身的推理与实现能力，而非提示工程的努力或编排设计。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate GNN-CB along two complementary tracks: a human-participant track (Section 3.2 ) with expert volunteers under standardized reproducibility constraints, and an LLM track (Section 3.3 ) with nine proprietary and open-source models under a frozen plan-then-code protocol with bounded execute-and-repair iterations. Both tracks use the same automated hidden-test pipeline and task-specific metrics: Macro-F1, accuracy, and AUC for classification, and MAE/NMAE for regression. We report human-cohort statistics, each LLM’s per-competition score and gap to the human top, and cross-task variability as a measure of consistency.

paragraphs.en: Table 2 and Figure 3 together summarize the performance of human participants across all 18 competitions. Overall, human performance exhibits variability across tasks, reflecting differences in task difficulty, graph structure, and domain complexity. Easy classification tasks (e.g., C03) achieve high scores with low variance, indicating that standard GNN pipelines are implemented reliably when task specifications are clear. In contrast, harder competitions (e.g., C02, C04, C18) show lower performance and larger gaps between best and worst submissions, reflecting higher sensitivity to architectural and optimization choices. Several medium-difficulty tasks (e.g., C09, C10) also exhibit notable variability, suggesting that engineering and training decisions remain critical even for relatively standard formulations. The two regression tasks (C14 and C17) display similar behaviour, with larger relative performance gaps and less stable convergence compared to most classification settings. These observations suggest that human participants perform consistently on conventional GNN problems but encounter increasing difficulty as tasks require more advanced graph reasoning, domain-specific adaptation, and complex optimization strategies.
paragraphs.zh: 表2和图3共同总结了人类参与者在全部18项竞赛中的表现。 总体而言，人类在不同任务上的表现存在差异，这反映了任务难度、图结构以及领域复杂性的不同。 简单的分类任务（例如 C03）能获得高分且方差较低，表明当任务说明清晰时，标准的 GNN 流程能够可靠地执行。 相比之下，难度更高的竞赛（例如 C02、C04、C18）表现更差，且最佳与最差提交结果之间的差距更大，反映出这些任务对架构和优化选择更为敏感。 一些中等难度的任务（例如 C09、C10）也表现出明显的差异，这表明即使对于相对标准的任务设定，工程实现和训练决策仍然至关重要。 两个回归任务（C14 和 C17）的表现类似，与大多数分类任务相比，其相对性能差距更大，收敛性也更不稳定。 这些观察结果表明，人类参与者在传统 GNN 问题上表现稳定，但随着任务需要更高级的图推理、领域特定适应和复杂的优化策略，其难度也会逐渐增加。

paragraphs.en: Table 3 reports the per-competition performance of the nine evaluated LLMs on all 18 GNN-CB tasks. The most important finding is that LLMs consistently fall short of Human Top performance across the benchmark under a zero-shot plan-then-code prompting protocol with a bounded execute-and-repair loop. Concretely, across all 9 evaluated models and 18 competition tasks (162 model–task pairs in total), LLMs surpass or tie the Human Top score in only 19 cases. In other words, in more than 88% of model–task pairs, the evaluated LLM does not reach Human Top performance. Among models achieving Human Top-level performance, we observe no clear model-family advantage, and the Human-Top level performance counts are roughly proportional to the number of models in each family. In addition, the average LLM performance exceeds the average human performance in only 6 of 16 competitions (37.5%), as shown in Figure 13 , meaning that average human performance remains higher on most competitions under this protocol.

paragraphs.en: We further examined severe underperformance in classification competitions, defined as scoring at least 30 percentage points below the best-performing LLM on the same task. paragraphs.en: The findings in Table 3 and Figure 4 reveal the core limitations of LLMs as autonomous GNN engineers under the evaluated setting. All evaluated models show substantial variance across the 18 competitions, indicating limited transfer of GNN construction and reasoning strategies across heterogeneous settings.Proprietary models demonstrate better average gaps than their open-source counterparts, yet no meaningful difference emerges between reasoning and chat LLMs within either tier—suggesting that chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities do not confer a systematic advantage on GNN-specific tasks under our zero-shot, bounded-repair protocol. In addition, performance gaps widen on Hard tier competitions, which shows the inability of LLMs dealing with complex GNN-based tasks. These results suggest that task-aware model routing or ensembling may be more effective than scaling a single model. Competition-style evaluation also provides a discriminative measure of practical GNN coding ability and highlights the risks of deploying LLM-generated solutions without expert oversight.
paragraphs.zh: 表3和图4中的研究结果揭示了在评估设定下，大型语言模型（LLM）作为自主GNN工程师的核心局限性。 所有受评估的模型在18项竞赛中均表现出显著差异，表明GNN构建与推理策略在不同异构环境间的迁移能力有限。专有模型的平均性能差距优于其开源对应模型，但在两个层级中，推理型LLM与聊天型LLM之间均未显现出有意义的差异——这表明在我们的零样本、有限修复协议下，链式思维推理能力并未为特定GNN任务带来系统性的优势。 此外，在“困难”层级竞赛中，性能差距进一步拉大，这显示出LLM难以应对复杂的基于GNN的任务。 这些结果表明，针对具体任务的模型路由或集成方法可能比单纯扩大单一模型规模更为有效。 竞赛风格的评估还提供了衡量实际GNN编码能力的区分性指标，并凸显了未经专家监督而部署LLM生成解决方案所潜藏的风险。

paragraphs.en: We introduced GNN-CB , the first competition-based benchmark for evaluating humans and LLMs on GNN coding tasks. It comprises 18 human-designed competitions spanning diverse graph categories, domains, and difficulty tiers, evaluated through a unified hidden-test pipeline. Three complementary protocols govern competition design, controlled human evaluation, and frozen-prompt LLM evaluation with bounded execute-and-repair iterations across API-only and agent-based settings. Under this protocol, current LLMs fall short of expert performance on most tasks and exhibit inconsistent performance across heterogeneous graph-learning problems. As models and evaluation methods continue to improve, the competition-based design of GNN-CB offers a challenging, extensible, and practically grounded testbed that can continuously distinguish advances in autonomous GNN engineering. Its public benchmark and dynamic leaderboards support future evaluation, comparison, and hands-on GNN coding practice.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 GNN-CB，这是首个基于竞赛的基准测试，用于评估人类和大型语言模型（LLM）在 GNN 编码任务上的表现。 该基准包含 18 项由人类设计的竞赛，涵盖多样的图类别、领域和难度等级，并通过统一的隐藏测试流程进行评估。 三种互补的协议规范了竞赛设计、受控的人类评估以及固定提示 LLM 的评估，这些评估在仅使用 API 和基于智能体的设置中均受限于有限的执行与修复迭代次数。 在此协议下，当前的大型语言模型在大多数任务上未能达到专家水平，并且在异构图学习问题上表现出性能不一致。 随着模型和评估方法的持续改进，GNN-CB 的竞赛化设计提供了一个具有挑战性、可扩展且贴近实际应用的测试平台，能够持续区分自主 GNN 工程领域的进步。 其公开的基准测试和动态排行榜支持未来的评估、比较以及实际的 GNN 编码练习。

paragraphs.en: Due to API and compute-budget constraints, our LLM evaluation is limited to nine leading proprietary and open-source models across two execution modes (API-only and agent-based), and our human evaluation involves 13–17 expert volunteers per competition. The model and task selection was guided by a balance between inclusiveness and feasibility, aiming to cover diverse access types (proprietary vs. open-source), and model families (Claude, Gemini, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Kimi, DeepSeek) while maintaining reproducibility and accessibility for research groups with limited compute resources. We believe this setup provides a meaningful and representative evaluation of contemporary LLM capabilities on end-to-end GNN coding tasks, without requiring the extensive infrastructure typically available only to large industrial laboratories. Accordingly, our results should be interpreted as a broad and reproducible evaluation of contemporary LLM performance under the evaluated bounded-repair and agent-based protocols, rather than as an estimate of the maximum attainable performance of each model. Larger inference budgets, repeated sampling, and more advanced model-specific prompting or agentic pipelines may further improve performance and should be investigated in future work.

paragraphs.en: A further limitation concerns the enforceability of the human-track constraint. Although the protocol restricts LLM use to low-level utility assistance and requires detailed reproducibility logs, local use of external assistance cannot be perfectly instrumented. Therefore, this constraint should be interpreted as practically auditable rather than fully enforceable.

sents.en: Although the protocol restricts LLM use to low-level utility assistance and requires detailed reproducibility logs, local use of external assistance cannot be perfectly instrumented.
sents.zh: 尽管该协议将 LLM 的使用限制在低级别的实用辅助功能上，并要求提供详细的可重复性日志，但对外部辅助工具在本地使用的情况仍无法实现完全监控。

sents.en: Therefore, this constraint should be interpreted as practically auditable rather than fully enforceable.
sents.zh: 因此，这一约束应被理解为具有实际可审计性，而非完全可执行。

paragraphs.en: While GNN-CB covers a broad range of node-, edge-, and graph-level problems, certain emerging settings such as graph generation, quantum graph modelling, and self-supervised or reinforcement-learning paradigms are not included in the current release. The use of task-specific evaluation metrics (macro- F 1 F_{1} , accuracy, AUC, MAE, and NMAE) reflects the heterogeneity of real-world graph problems and limits direct cross-task comparison. To mitigate this, we report per-task gap-to-human-top scores and separate classification and regression results in our visualizations, particularly since the benchmark contains only two regression competitions. Although the two regression competitions broaden the task and metric diversity of GNN-CB , their limited number does not support strong general conclusions about LLM performance on graph-regression problems. Expanding both the number and diversity of regression competitions is therefore an important direction for future releases. Finally, because LLM capabilities evolve rapidly, the reported results represent model snapshots available as of May 2026, although the qualitative patterns we observe—difficulty stratification, the capability-versus-consistency gap, and family-level differences—are expected to remain informative as models continue to advance. These limitations can be viewed as opportunities for future extensions of GNN-CB toward broader graph-learning paradigms, larger model panels, and continuously updated evaluations.

paragraphs.en: The present study establishes GNN-CB as a zero-shot, frozen-prompt benchmark, and its infrastructure enables several deeper analyses that we did not pursue here due to computational and budgetary constraints. On the modelling side, future work can measure how performance scales beyond the current zero-shot protocol through few-shot prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and task-specific fine-tuning, and can characterise stochastic variability via repeated sampling, confidence intervals, and pass@ k k -style metrics rather than the single greedy run reported here. Because every submission is executed and validated, the benchmark also supports a fine-grained error-mode taxonomy—incorrect graph construction, invalid message-passing architectures, preprocessing data leakage, mishandled class imbalance, and malformed submissions—that would reveal where and why LLMs break down beyond aggregate scores.
paragraphs.zh: 本研究确立了 GNN-CB 作为一个零样本、固定提示的基准测试，其基础设施支持多种更深入的分析，但由于计算和预算限制，我们在此并未展开这些分析。 在建模方面，未来的研究可以通过少样本提示、检索增强生成以及任务特定的微调，来衡量性能在当前零样本协议之外的扩展情况；此外，还可通过重复采样、置信区间以及 pass@k 类指标（而非本文报告的单次贪心运行）来描述其随机波动性。 由于每次提交都会被执行和验证，该基准测试还支持一种精细的错误模式分类——包括错误的图构建、无效的消息传递架构、预处理数据泄露、不当处理的类别不平衡问题以及格式错误的提交——这将有助于揭示大型语言模型在哪些方面、因何原因出现失效，而不仅仅是依赖汇总分数。

paragraphs.en: On the evaluation side, the logged execution and repair traces enable a detailed token-economy and cost–latency analysis, particularly contrasting the per-call budget of API-only runs with the multi-step session budget of agent-based runs, alongside an analysis of agentic depth (tool-call counts, repair-loop depth, and the contribution of extended chain-of-thought). Rigour can be further strengthened through paired significance testing, bootstrap confidence intervals, and rank-correlation analysis of the human–LLM ordering. Finally, as a living benchmark with automated infrastructure and dynamic leaderboards, GNN-CB can be extended to broader paradigms (graph generation, self-supervised, temporal, and reinforcement-learning formulations) and used longitudinally to track whether the capability–consistency gap narrows as new models are released.
paragraphs.zh: 在评估方面，记录的执行和修复轨迹能够支持对令牌经济性和成本-延迟的深入分析，尤其可以对比仅使用 API 的运行中每次调用的预算与基于智能体的运行中的多步骤会话预算，同时还能分析智能体深度（工具调用次数、修复循环深度以及扩展思维链的贡献）。 通过配对显著性检验、自助置信区间以及对人类-LLM排序的秩相关分析，可以进一步增强研究的严谨性。 最后，作为一个具备自动化基础设施和动态排行榜的动态基准测试，GNN-CB 可扩展至更广泛的模式（图生成、自监督、时序和强化学习形式），并可用于长期追踪，以观察随着新模型发布，能力与一致性之间的差距是否正在缩小。

paragraphs.en: GNN-CB evaluates LLM-generated GNN code that, if deployed in safety-critical domains such as medical diagnosis, financial-fraud detection, or neuroimaging without expert verification, could amplify model failures or propagate dataset biases. We release the benchmark for controlled research and hands-on GNN coding practice, and discourage direct deployment of LLM-generated solutions without expert review.
paragraphs.zh: GNN-CB 评估由 LLM 生成的 GNN 代码；如果未经专家验证便将其部署在医疗诊断、金融欺诈检测或神经影像等安全关键领域，这些代码可能会放大模型故障或传播数据集中的偏见。 我们发布该基准用于受控研究和实际的 GNN 编码练习，并不建议在没有专家审查的情况下直接使用 LLM 生成的解决方案。

paragraphs.en: This appendix provides detailed descriptions of the competitions included in GNN-CB , each following a standardized structure (task definition, dataset statistics, evaluation metric, and submission protocol) and a unified evaluation pipeline based on hidden test sets, secure submission handling, and automated GitHub Actions scoring to ensure reproducibility and fairness.

paragraphs.en: The benchmark spans a diverse set of graph problem categories, including homogeneous , heterogeneous , temporal , spatial , hierarchical , molecular , and generalization graphs. To fomally define, Homogeneous : Graph with uniform node and edge types, Heterogeneous : Graph with multiple node and edge type, Temporal : Graph changes over time, Spatial : Graph is embedded in a spatial domain where nodes and edges reflect physical or geometric proximity, Hierarchical : Graph with multi-level structure among nodes, Molecular : Graph represents molecular structures, where nodes are atoms and edges are chemical bonds, Generalization : Test graph is drawn from distributions different from the training graph.
paragraphs.zh: 该基准测试涵盖了多种图问题类别，包括同构图、异构图、时序图、空间图、层次图、分子图和泛化图。 为正式定义这些概念：同构图：节点和边类型均统一的图；异构图：包含多种节点和边类型的图；时序图：随时间变化的图；空间图：嵌入在空间域中的图，其中节点和边反映物理或几何上的邻近关系；层次图：节点间具有多级结构的图；分子图：表示分子结构的图，其中节点是原子，边是化学键；泛化图：测试图从与训练图不同的分布中抽取。

paragraphs.en: Across all competitions, a unified submission and evaluation protocol is enforced to ensure fairness, reproducibility, and consistent leaderboard construction. Each participant is allowed a single final submission per competition version, and only the latest valid submission is considered for evaluation. Submissions that are not properly encrypted, fail decryption, or do not conform to the required format are automatically rejected and excluded from scoring. Leaderboard ranking follows a Kaggle-style tie-breaking rule, where identical scores are assigned the same rank, and no additional ordering is enforced between tied entries.
paragraphs.zh: 在所有竞赛中，均强制执行统一的提交与评估协议，以确保公平性、可重复性以及排行榜构建的一致性。 每位参赛者每个竞赛版本仅允许提交一次最终结果，且只有最新的有效提交才会被纳入评估。 未正确加密、解密失败或不符合规定格式的提交将被自动拒绝，并排除在评分之外。 排行榜排名遵循 Kaggle 风格的同分处理规则：分数相同的条目将获得相同的排名，且不会在并列条目之间施加额外的排序。

paragraphs.en: The dataset comprises street networks for 120 cities distributed across North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, and Central Asia, extracted from OpenStreetMap via OSMnx within a 500 m buffer around each city centre and restricted to driveable roads. The class distribution reflects naturally occurring urban patterns and is moderately imbalanced, with 37 grid, 31 organic, and 52 hybrid cities. Each graph retains node coordinates, edge geometries and lengths, and graph-level attributes such as the city name and layout type; for the evaluation split, the layout label is withheld. paragraphs.en: GNN_BACE (BACE Inhibition Prediction) is a graph-level binary classification task whose primary objective is to predict whether a given molecule acts as an inhibitor of the β \beta -secretase 1 (BACE-1) enzyme, a critical target in Alzheimer’s disease research. Formally, the objective is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( G k ) → y k f(G_{k})\rightarrow y_{k} for each molecule represented as molecular graphs G k = ( V k , E k ) G_{k}=(V_{k},E_{k}) . Molecules are represented as undirected graphs G k = ( V k , E k ) G_{k}=(V_{k},E_{k}) , where nodes correspond to atoms and edges correspond to chemical bonds. Each node is described by an 8-dimensional one-hot atom-type feature vector, while edges include simple bond-level attributes. Label is 1 1 for active inhibitors and inactive compounds as 0 0 .
paragraphs.zh: GNN_BACE（BACE 抑制预测）是一项图级别的二元分类任务，其主要目标是预测给定分子是否为 β-分泌酶 1（BACE-1）的抑制剂，而 BACE-1 是阿尔茨海默病研究中的一个关键靶点。 从形式化角度而言，其目标是为每个以分子图 G_k = (V_k, E_k) 表示的分子学习一个映射 f(G_k) → y_k。 分子被表示为无向图 G_k = (V_k, E_k)，其中节点对应原子，边对应化学键。 每个节点由一个 8 维的一热原子类型特征向量描述，而边则包含简单的键级别属性。 标签为 1 时表示活性抑制剂，非活性化合物则为 0。

paragraphs.en: The GRAPE ( G raph R etinal A nalysis for P rediction and E valuation) challenge is a graph-level classification benchmark designed for diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection from retinal vessel graphs. Each sample corresponds to a retinal vascular network represented as a spatial graph G k = ( V k , E k ) G_{k}=(V_{k},E_{k}) , where nodes denote vessel bifurcation or intersection points and edges represent vessel segments connecting them. Given a collection of retinal graphs 𝒢 = { G k } \mathcal{G}=\{G_{k}\} , the objective is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( G k ) → y k f(G_{k})\rightarrow y_{k} that predicts whether the retinal image corresponds to a healthy subject ( 0 0 ) or a diabetic retinopathy patient ( 1 1 ).

The dataset is partitioned into 55 training graphs and 15 hidden test graphs using stratified sampling to preserve class proportions across splits. Each retinal graph preserves the vascular connectivity structure derived from vessel segmentation outputs.
paragraphs.zh: 该基准数据集由从三个公开可用的视网膜成像数据集（DRIVE、STARE 和 HRF）中提取的视网膜血管图构建而成。 该数据集总共包含 70 个图，其中 48 个为健康案例，22 个为糖尿病视网膜病变案例。 具体而言，DRIVE 子集贡献了 20 个图（17 个健康案例，3 个糖尿病视网膜病变案例），STARE 贡献了 20 个图（16 个健康案例，4 个糖尿病视网膜病变案例），HRF 贡献了 30 个图（15 个健康案例，15 个糖尿病视网膜病变案例）。 该数据集通过分层抽样划分为 55 个训练图和 15 个隐藏测试图，以确保各划分部分中类别比例保持一致。 每个视网膜图都保留了源自血管分割结果的血管连接结构。

paragraphs.en: The Liar Nodes challenge is formulated as a transductive node classification problem over a homogenous graph derived from single-cell cancer transcriptomics data. Each node represents an individual cell, while graph edges encode contextual or biological similarity relationships between cells within the tumor microenvironment. Given a graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , the objective is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i} that predicts whether a cell is cancerous or non-cancerous.
paragraphs.zh: “说谎者节点”挑战被表述为一个传递性节点分类问题，该问题基于从单细胞癌症转录组学数据中导出的均匀图。 每个节点代表一个单独细胞，而图中的边则编码了肿瘤微环境中细胞之间的上下文或生物学相似性关系。 给定一个图 G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E)，目标在于学习一个映射 f⁡(v_i)→y_i，以预测某个细胞是否为癌细胞或非癌细胞。

paragraphs.en: The underlying data originate from the Cancer Single-cell Expression Map (CancerSCEM) resource [ Zeng et al., 2022 ] , which contains large-scale single-cell RNA sequencing data across multiple cancer types. The original dataset provides UMI count matrices, cell-type annotations, functional molecular descriptors, and cell-cell interaction information. For the purposes of this benchmark, the data are transformed into graph learning instances suitable for GNN training and evaluation. Node embeddings are intentionally altered and partially corrupted in order to create contradictions between intrinsic node representations and graph context.
paragraphs.zh: 底层数据源自癌症单细胞表达图谱（CancerSCEM）资源 [Zeng et al., 2022]，该资源包含多种癌症类型的大规模单细胞 RNA 测序数据。 原始数据集提供了 UMI 计数矩阵、细胞类型标注、功能分子描述符以及细胞间相互作用信息。 在本基准测试中，数据被转换为适用于 GNN 训练和评估的图学习实例。 节点嵌入被有意修改并部分损坏，以在内在节点表示与图上下文之间制造矛盾。

paragraphs.en: The GraphFMD ( Graph -based F inancial M isconduct D etection) challenge is a temporal inductive node classification task defined over the Bitcoin transaction network. Each sample is a transaction represented as a node v i v_{i} in a directed temporal graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , where nodes denote individual Bitcoin transactions and edges denote the flow of Bitcoin between them. The objective is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i} that assigns each test-time transaction to one of two classes: illicit (1) or licit (2).
paragraphs.zh: GraphFMD（基于图的金融欺诈检测）挑战是一项在比特币交易网络上定义的时序归纳式节点分类任务。 每个样本都是一个交易，表示为有向时序图 G = ( V , E ) 中的一个节点 v i v_{i}，其中节点代表单个比特币交易，边代表比特币在它们之间的流动。 目标是为每个测试时的交易学习一个映射 f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i}，将其归入两个类别之一：非法（1）或合法（2）。

paragraphs.en: The dataset is derived from the Elliptic Bitcoin transaction graph Weber et al. [2019] and is partitioned temporally: training nodes span time steps 1–34, comprising 16,658 labelled transactions, while test nodes are drawn from time steps 35 and beyond, comprising 8,896 transactions. The graph contains approximately 5 million directed edges. Each node is associated with a 165-dimensional feature vector consisting of 94 local transaction features (e.g., transaction amounts, fees, and input/output counts) and 71 aggregated neighbourhood features derived from one-hop neighbours; Gaussian noise has been injected into these features to simulate real-world data degradation. The dataset exhibits strong class imbalance, with illicit transactions constituting only 1–3% of all nodes.
paragraphs.zh: 该数据集源自 Weber 等人提出的 Elliptic 比特币交易图 [2019]。 该数据集按时间划分：训练节点覆盖第 1–34 个时间步，包含 16,658 个带标签的交易；测试节点则取自第 35 个时间步及之后的数据，包含 8,896 笔交易。 该图包含约 500 万条有向边。 每个节点都关联一个 165 维特征向量，由 94 个局部交易特征（例如交易金额、手续费以及输入/输出数量）和从一跳邻居中获取的 71 个聚合邻域特征组成；这些特征中已注入高斯噪声，以模拟真实世界中的数据退化现象。 该数据集存在严重的类别不平衡问题，非法交易仅占所有节点的 1%–3%。

paragraphs.en: The PARK-GNN Challenge ( P arkinson’s A coustic R epresentation & K nowledge with G raph N eural N etworks) is a transductive node classification task defined over a homogenous graph constructed from acoustic voice recordings. Each node v i v_{i} in the graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) represents a single voice recording, characterized by a 22-dimensional feature vector of acoustic measurements including vocal fundamental frequency statistics, jitter and shimmer variations, harmonics-to-noise ratios, and nonlinear dynamical complexity features. Edges are formed by a k k -nearest-neighbor criterion ( k = 5 k=5 ) over acoustic similarity in feature space, supplemented by subject-level connections that link recordings from the same individual. The objective is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i ∈ { 0 , 1 } f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i}\in\{0,1\} that assigns each voice recording to either a healthy control (0) or a Parkinson’s Disease patient (1).

paragraphs.en: The GNN-CoRA (Cora Node Classification Challenge) competition is a node classification task defined over a homogenous citation-network graph derived from the Cora benchmark dataset [ Sen et al., 2008 ] . The objective is to train a GNN that predicts the research-topic label of each publication node from both its textual feature representation and the surrounding citation structure. Formally, given a graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) in which nodes correspond to publications and edges denote citation relationships, the task is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i} that assigns each node v i v_{i} to one of seven research-topic classes.

paragraphs.en: The GTA ( G raph T opology Ablation ) challenge is formulated as a supervised binary graph classification problem over molecular graphs derived from the MUTAG dataset, a widely used benchmark in chemical informatics. Each graph G k = ( V k , E k ) G_{k}=(V_{k},E_{k}) represents a chemical compound in which nodes correspond to atoms and edges correspond to chemical bonds. The objective is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( G k ) → y k f(G_{k})\rightarrow y_{k} that predicts whether a molecule is mutagenic or non-mutagenic with respect to Salmonella typhimurium . The dataset contains 188 molecular graphs with an average of approximately 18 nodes and 40 edges per graph. Node attributes consist of categorical atom labels interpreted as node features.

paragraphs.en: OctoNode Cup (GitHub Social Network Classification) is a transductive node classification task focused on classifying users in a homogenous GitHub social network. In this network, represented as a graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , each node corresponds to a GitHub user and edges represent connections between users. The task aims to predict a binary label for each node based on its associated features. paragraphs.en: The Graph4ASD (Graph Neural Networks for the classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder) challenge is a binary graph classification task over brain networks derived from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) recordings of the human brain. paragraphs.en: The dataset is drawn from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) Craddock et al. [2013] , a multi-site repository of anonymised rs-fMRI scans collected at seventeen international acquisition sites. The full corpus contains 1,009 subjects (516 ASD, 51.14%; 493 controls, 48.86%), yielding a near-balanced two-class distribution. Each subject’s brain volume is parcellated with the Craddock 200 atlas, so every graph has exactly n = 200 n=200 nodes corresponding to predefined regions of interest, with identical node ordering across samples. A challenge-specific subset, preprocessed exclusively for this benchmark, is partitioned into 484 training and 153 evaluation graphs; participants are required to use the data as released, without alternative preprocessing pipelines or auxiliary neuroimaging corpora.

paragraphs.en: Mix2Print (Learning Material Interaction Physics for identifying parameters of 3D Bioprinting) is a graph regression challenge focused on predicting optimal 3D bioprinting parameters from bioink formulation graphs. The competition models each bioink formulation as a homogenous graph, where nodes correspond to biomaterials and edges represent potential interactions between materials in the mixture. The task aims to learn the underlying material interaction physics governing extrusion-based bioprinting.
paragraphs.zh: Mix2Print（用于识别 3D 生物打印参数的材料相互作用物理模型）是一项图回归挑战，旨在根据生物墨水配方图预测最佳的 3D 生物打印参数。 该竞赛将每种生物墨水配方建模为均匀图，其中节点对应生物材料，边表示混合物中材料之间潜在相互作用。 该任务旨在学习控制挤出式生物打印的底层材料相互作用物理规律。

paragraphs.zh: 给定一个图结构 G i = ( V i , E i , X i ) G_{i}=(V_{i},E_{i},X_{i})，参与者需要预测三个连续目标：f ⁡ ( G i ) → y i f(G_{i})\rightarrow y_{i}，其中 y i = ( pressure , temperature , speed ) y_{i}=(\text{压力},\text{温度},\text{速度})，分别对应压力（kPa），表示挤出力；温度（∘ C），表示打印温度；以及速度（mm/s），表示打印头速度。

paragraphs.en: The dataset represents bioink formulations as fully connected graphs, reflecting the assumption that all biomaterials in a formulation can potentially interact with each other. Node features consist of one-hot encoded material identity features and normalized concentration value. Thus, the total node feature dimensionality is approximately D ≈ 31 D\approx 31 . The dataset contains 423 bioink formulations collected from peer-reviewed publications, 30 biomaterials appearing at least five times ,303 training samples and 120 test samples. The train-test split follows a stratified grouping strategy based on printing temperature regimes (hydrogel versus thermoplastic formulations). The dataset captures diverse biomaterial categories including alginates, gelatins, polymers, ceramics, and natural biomaterials.
paragraphs.zh: 该数据集将生物墨水配方表示为全连接图，反映了这样一种假设：配方中的所有生物材料都可能相互相互作用。 节点特征由独热编码的材料身份特征和归一化的浓度值组成。 因此，总节点特征维度约为 D ≈ 31。 该数据集包含从经过同行评审的出版物中收集的 423 种生物墨水配方，其中 30 种生物材料至少出现过五次，并包含 303 个训练样本和 120 个测试样本。 训练集与测试集的划分遵循基于打印温度范围（水凝胶与热塑性配方）的分层分组策略。 该数据集涵盖了多种生物材料类别，包括藻酸盐、明胶、聚合物、陶瓷和天然生物材料。

paragraphs.en: THInC ( T umor H istopathology In ductive C lassification) is formulated as an inductive node classification problem over spatial cell graphs derived from H&E-stained histology images. Each graph G k = ( V k , E k ) G_{k}=(V_{k},E_{k}) corresponds to a single patient or tissue slide, where nodes represent individual cell nuclei and edges encode spatial relationships between nearby cells. Given a set of training graphs 𝒢 t ​ r ​ a ​ i ​ n \mathcal{G}_{train} , the goal is to learn a mapping f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i} that assigns each cell to one of four classes: Tumor (0), Stromal (1), Lymphocyte (2), or Macrophage (3). Importantly, predictions must generalize to entirely unseen graphs corresponding to new patients, making this an inductive rather than transductive learning setting.
paragraphs.zh: THInC（肿瘤组织病理学归纳分类）被构建为一个归纳性节点分类问题，其输入是从 H&E 染色的组织学图像中提取的空间细胞图。 每个图 G k = ( V k , E k ) G_{k}=(V_{k},E_{k}) 对应于单个患者或组织切片，其中节点代表单个细胞核，边则编码邻近细胞之间的空间关系。 给定一组训练图 𝒢 t ​ r ​ a ​ i ​ n \mathcal{G}_{train} ，目标是为每个细胞分配一个属于四类之一的标签：肿瘤（0）、间质（1）、淋巴细胞（2）或巨噬细胞（3），从而学习一个映射 f ⁡ ( v i ) → y i f(v_{i})\rightarrow y_{i}。 重要的是，预测必须能够泛化到完全未见过的新患者所对应的图，因此这是一个归纳学习场景，而非外推学习场景。

paragraphs.en: The dataset is derived from the NuCLS breast cancer histopathology dataset [ Amgad et al., 2022 ] and is transformed into spatial cell graphs using a biologically grounded pipeline. Starting from raw histology images, cell nuclei are detected and represented as bounding boxes, which are then converted into centroid coordinates ( x , y ) (x,y) forming graph nodes. Graph edges are constructed using a k k -nearest neighbor (k-NN) approach with k = 5 k=5 , where each cell is connected to its closest spatial neighbors within the same tissue image.
paragraphs.zh: 该数据集源自 NuCLS 乳腺癌组织病理学数据集 [Amgad et al., 2022]，并通过一种基于生物学原理的流程转换为空间细胞图。 从原始组织学图像开始，首先检测细胞核并将其表示为边界框，随后将这些边界框转换为质心坐标 (x, y)，从而形成图中的节点。 图的边通过 k 最近邻（k-NN）方法构建，其中 k = 5；在此方法中，每个细胞都与同一组织图像中最邻近的空间相邻细胞相连。

paragraphs.en: The inductive split is performed at the image level rather than the node level. Specifically, 80% of tissue images are used for training, while the remaining 20% are held out as completely unseen test patients. Node features consist of normalized spatial coordinates ( x , y ) (x,y) along with morphological descriptors such as nucleus width and height, standardized to zero mean and unit variance to ensure stable training.

paragraphs.en: This appendix provides additional implementation details for the human evaluation track of GNN-CB .
paragraphs.zh: 本附录提供了 GNN-CB 人类评估部分的更多实现细节。

paragraphs.en: All human participants follow a uniform implementation protocol designed to ensure reproducibility, prevent test-set leakage, and isolate model design choices as the primary source of performance variation across submissions. Each competition enforces a fixed wall-clock budget of three hours of CPU time per task, with hyperparameter tuning capped at five training runs per task and a single final submission per benchmark version to discourage test-set overfitting. All random seeds are fixed to seed = 25 , training loss curves must be plotted to verify proper convergence and detect overfitting (with early stopping permitted), and the exact source code that produced each submitted prediction file is retained alongside the recorded training time and hardware specifications.
paragraphs.zh: 所有人类参与者均遵循统一的实施协议，该协议旨在确保可重复性、防止测试集泄露，并将模型设计选择隔离为各提交方案间性能差异的主要来源。 每场比赛强制执行固定的实际运行时间限制：每个任务最多使用三小时 CPU 时间，超参数调整以每个任务最多五次训练轮次为限，且每个基准版本仅允许提交一次最终结果，以避免对测试集过度拟合。 所有随机种子均固定为 seed = 25，必须绘制训练损失曲线以验证收敛正常并检测过拟合（允许提前停止），同时保留生成每个已提交预测文件的精确源代码，并与记录的训练时间和硬件规格一并存档。

paragraphs.en: Submitted solutions must be implemented using Graph Neural Network architectures only; convolutional, recurrent, and other non-graph spatial deep-learning models are prohibited, and copy-pasting external solutions is not permitted. LLM assistance is restricted to low-level utility functions and must not expose the model to any task-specific information (e.g., competition name, dataset identity, or feature schema) that could induce data leakage. For each competition, every participant maintains a single documentation file containing the hyperparameter-search strategy used (manual, grid, or random), all configurations attempted within the five-run budget, and the exact prompts and LLM-generated snippets reused in the solution. Together, these records provide a post-hoc audit trail for verifying that the submitted prediction file is consistent with the declared GNN-based solution, documented hyperparameter search, and permitted low-level LLM assistance.
paragraphs.zh: 提交的解决方案必须仅使用图神经网络架构实现；禁止使用卷积、循环及其他非图结构的空间深度学习模型，也不允许复制粘贴外部解决方案。 LLM 的协助仅限于低级别工具函数，且不得向模型暴露任何与任务相关的特定信息（例如竞赛名称、数据集身份或特征模式），以免引发数据泄露。 对于每场竞赛，每位参赛者必须维护一个唯一的文档文件，其中包含所采用的超参数搜索策略（手动、网格或随机）、在五次运行预算内尝试的所有配置，以及解决方案中重复使用的精确提示和 LLM 生成的代码片段。 这些记录共同构成事后审计追踪，用于验证提交的预测文件是否与声明的基于 GNN 的解决方案、已记录的超参数搜索过程以及允许的低级别 LLM 协助保持一致。

paragraphs.en: Figure 5 summarizes the composition of the 18 GNN-CB competitions attempted by human participants across four characterizing dimensions: graph category, difficulty tier, task type, and application domain. The benchmark is dominated by homogeneous graphs ( 55.6 % 55.6\% ), with the remainder distributed across spatial, generalization, temporal, heterogeneous, hierarchical, and molecular settings. Difficulty tiers are skewed toward Medium ( 44.4 % 44.4\% ) and Hard ( 38.9 % 38.9\% ) competitions, with only three Easy tasks. Node classification and graph classification together account for 83.3 % 83.3\% of the tasks, complemented by one edge-prediction and two graph-regression competitions. Application domains span medical, biomedical, academic, neuroimaging, social, bioinformatics, bioprinting, cybersecurity, finance, and urban data, reflecting the benchmark’s emphasis on real-world heterogeneity rather than a single application focus.

paragraphs.en: GNN-CB draws on a globally distributed cohort of human contributors. Figure 6 shows the locations of the 18 participating universities across 12 countries spanning four continents, with each country annotated by the competition(s) co-designed by its contributing team(s). The cohort represents Africa (Algeria, Egypt, Ghana, Tunisia, Uganda), the Americas (Peru, USA), Asia (India, Nepal, Pakistan), and Europe (Turkey, UK), reflecting the benchmark’s emphasis on broad geographic and institutional representation rather than concentration in a single research hub. This geographic diversity is intentional: it ensures that the curated competitions, datasets, and domain conventions in GNN-CB are not dominated by the priorities of any single regional research community, and that the human performance baseline reported in Table 2 reflects a heterogeneous expert pool rather than a homogeneous local cohort.
paragraphs.zh: GNN-CB 依托一个全球分布的人类贡献者群体。 图 6 展示了来自 12 个国家、横跨四大洲的 18 所参与大学的位置，每个国家都标注了其贡献团队共同设计的竞赛。 该群体涵盖了非洲（阿尔及利亚、埃及、加纳、突尼斯、乌干达）、美洲（秘鲁、美国）、亚洲（印度、尼泊尔、巴基斯坦）和欧洲（土耳其、英国），体现了该基准测试对广泛地理和机构代表性的重视，而非集中于单一研究枢纽。 这种地理多样性是有意设计的：它确保了 GNN-CB 中精心挑选的竞赛、数据集和领域惯例不会由任何单一地区研究社区的优先事项所主导，并且表 2 中报告的人类性能基准反映的是一个异质化的专家群体，而非一个同质化的本地群体。

paragraphs.en: To assess the comparative performance of leading LLMs against human baselines, we evaluate their capabilities across Easy, Medium, and Hard classification tasks in the GNN-CB benchmark from three perspectives: a gap analysis quantifying performance differences relative to the human-top score, an average human–LLM comparison, and a category-based comparison of how different model types perform across difficulty levels.
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估主流大型语言模型（LLM）相较于人类基准的表现差异，我们从三个角度对它们在 GNN-CB 基准中“简单”、“中等”和“困难”分类任务上的能力进行了评估：一是通过差距分析量化其性能与人类最高分之间的差异；二是进行人类与 LLM 的平均表现对比；三是基于类别比较不同模型类型在各个难度等级上的表现。

paragraphs.en: For Easy classification tasks (Figure 10 ), proprietary models except from GPT 5.4 Codex show minimal deviation, with best-case gaps approaching zero and worst-case gaps remaining moderate. In contrast, open-source models exhibit larger negative gaps across all models, indicating instability and weaker alignment with human-top performance. On Medium tasks (Figure 11 ), the performance gap widens across all model categories. Proprietary models continue to outperform open-source models in terms of mean gap and exhibit more consistent behavior overall, whereas open-source models show substantially larger negative gaps and higher variability across competitions.
paragraphs.zh: 对于简单的分类任务（图 10），除 GPT 5.4 Codex 外的专有模型表现差异极小，最佳情况下的差距接近于零，最坏情况下的差距也保持在中等水平。 相比之下，开源模型在所有模型中均表现出更大的负向差距，这表明其稳定性较差，且与人类顶尖水平的契合度更弱。 在中难度任务中（图 11），所有模型类别的性能差距都进一步拉大。 在平均差距方面，专有模型持续优于开源模型，并且整体表现更为稳定；而开源模型则表现出明显更大的负向差距，并在各项竞赛中的波动性更高。

paragraphs.en: Figure 13 analyzes LLM and human average scores across Easy, Medium, and Hard competitions on a per-competition basis. Although LLM averages occasionally surpass human averages on individual competitions, humans still achieve higher average scores in 10 out of the 16 classification competitions, indicating that human participants remain more consistently reliable overall. Moreover, as task difficulty increases from Easy to Hard, LLM performance declines similarly to human performance, with larger drops observed on harder tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 图 13 按每项竞赛分别分析了 LLM 和人类在简单、中等和困难竞赛中的平均得分。 尽管 LLM 的平均得分在某些单项竞赛中偶尔会超过人类的平均得分，但在 16 项分类竞赛中，人类仍有 10 项的平均得分更高，这表明人类参与者在整体上仍然更为稳定可靠。 此外，随着任务难度从简单到困难逐步提升，LLM 的表现也如同人类一样出现下降，且难度越高的任务中下降幅度越大。

paragraphs.en: Finally, we analyse model performance by category across the Easy, Medium, and Hard classification tasks using each model’s best, mean, and worst accuracy. On Easy tasks (Figure 14 ), proprietary models achieve high performance with a small variablity between best and worst scores, indicating strong consistency, while open-source models remain competitive but display wider variability. On Medium and Hard tasks (Figures 15 and 16 ), mean scores decline across nearly all models and the best–worst variance widens, indicating reduced stability as complexity increases. The steep decline in mean and worst-case accuracy highlights the limitations of current foundational architectures under higher complexity.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，我们根据每个模型的最佳、平均和最差准确率，按类别分析模型在“简单”、“中等”和“困难”分类任务中的性能。 在“简单”任务中（图 14），专有模型表现优异，且最佳与最差分数之间的差异很小，表明其一致性很强；而开源模型虽仍具竞争力，但表现出更大的波动性。 在“中等”和“困难”任务中（图 15 和图 16），几乎所有模型的平均得分均有所下降，且最佳与最差分数的差异也扩大，表明随着复杂度的增加，稳定性有所降低。 平均准确率和最差准确率的大幅下降，凸显了当前基础架构在更高复杂度任务下的局限性。

paragraphs.en: Severe underperformance was concentrated primarily among open-source models: 17 of the 20 cases (85%) were produced by open-source LLMs, compared with only three (15%) by proprietary models. When normalized by the number of evaluated model–task pairs, severe failures occurred in 17/64 (26.6%) open-source pairs and 3/80 (3.8%) proprietary pairs. Chat models accounted for 14 cases and reasoning models for six, corresponding to failure rates of 14/80 (17.5%) and 6/64 (9.4%), respectively. However, given the small and unbalanced number of models across categories, particularly the presence of only one open-source reasoning model, these differences should be interpreted as descriptive patterns rather than inherent effects of model family or accessibility.

paragraphs.en: This research was carried out as part of the BASIRA Lab Global Consortia Projects within the GNNs for Rising Stars Program , which Dr Rekik founded, organized, and taught, and which gave the authors their shared foundation in graph representation learning and directly shaped the design of the competitions presented here; further details on the program and its competitions are available at https://basiralab.github.io/GNN-CB/ . We are grateful to have carried out this work as a global consortium of early-career researchers spanning 24 institutions across 16 countries.
paragraphs.zh: 本研究是 BASIRA Lab 全球合作计划项目的一部分，该项目属于“GNNs for Rising Stars”计划。该计划由 Rekik 博士发起、组织并授课，为作者们奠定了图表示学习领域的共同基础，并直接影响了本文所介绍竞赛的设计；有关该计划及其竞赛的更多详情，请访问 https://basiralab.github.io/GNN-CB/ 。 我们深感荣幸，能与来自 16 个国家、24 家机构的早期职业研究人员组成一个全球性合作团队，共同开展这项工作。
